content: Hydralazine is a medication that can be prescribed for conditions other than high blood pressure, as determined by your healthcare provider. It works by relaxing the blood vessels in your body, which allows blood to flow more easily and reduces blood pressure. Lowering blood pressure is crucial to prevent complications such as heart or kidney problems, as well as to reduce the risk of stroke or heart attack. Hydralazine is available in several dosage forms for oral administration, including 10 mg, 25 mg, 50 mg, and 100 mg tablets. It is also available in injectable forms. The medication should be stored at room temperature, between 68°F and 77°F (20°C to 25°C), but it can tolerate short-term exposure to temperatures between 59°F and 86°F (15°C to 30°C), such as during transportation. It should be kept in a cool, dry place, tightly closed, and out of reach of children. Hydralazine can be administered as a liquid injection into a blood vessel or muscle, or as a tablet that is swallowed. Common side effects include headache, decreased appetite, nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, a pounding or fast heartbeat, and chest pain or discomfort. If any of these side effects bother you, inform your healthcare provider. There may be other side effects not listed here, so contact your healthcare provider if you suspect you are experiencing an adverse reaction. Serious side effects of hydralazine, though less common, include lupus-like symptoms, chest pain, blood disorders, and nerve problems. Lupus-like symptoms may include rash, joint pain, fever, weakness, swollen glands, reduced need to urinate, pink or red urine, and swelling. If you experience any of these, contact your healthcare provider immediately. Chest pain caused by hydralazine can be a sign of a heart attack, especially in individuals with pre-existing heart disease. Seek emergency medical help if you experience chest pain or pressure, a fast or abnormal heartbeat, trouble breathing, pain in your back, jaw, throat, or arm, sweating, nausea, vomiting, or dizziness. Hydralazine can also cause blood disorders such as agranulocytosis, anemia, or low white blood cell count (leukopenia). Symptoms of blood disorders include fever, shortness of breath, pale or yellowish skin, easy bruising or bleeding, frequent infections, unusual weakness or tiredness, dizziness, or feeling faint. If you notice any of these symptoms, contact your healthcare provider immediately. Additionally, hydralazine may cause peripheral neuropathy, which is nerve damage that can result in abnormal sensations or weakness. Certain individuals should not use hydralazine. This includes people allergic to hydralazine, Apresoline, or any of the ingredients in the specific product. Your pharmacist can provide a list of ingredients if needed. Hydralazine should not be used in individuals with coronary artery disease (CAD) or mitral valvular rheumatic heart disease, as it can worsen these conditions by increasing the workload on the heart. Before using hydralazine, ensure it has been prescribed by a healthcare provider and take it exactly as directed. Do not share this medication with others, even if they have the same condition, as it may harm them. Hydralazine can affect your alertness or coordination, so avoid driving or performing activities requiring focus until you know how the medication affects you. Inform your healthcare provider about all your health conditions, including heart disease, kidney disease, stroke, or a history of rheumatic fever. Also, disclose all prescription and over-the-counter medications, vitamins, minerals, herbal products, and supplements you are taking, as hydralazine may interact with other substances. If you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding, discuss this with your healthcare provider, as hydralazine passes into breast milk and its effects on pregnancy are not fully understood. There are no known interactions between hydralazine and foods or nonalcoholic drinks. However, it is unclear if alcohol consumption affects hydralazine. Drinking alcohol while taking hydralazine may increase the risk of dizziness. If you or someone else accidentally takes too much hydralazine, seek medical help immediately by calling 911 or contacting a Poison Control Center at 800-222-1222. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. If it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and take only the next scheduled dose. Do not take double or extra doses. Hydralazine is commonly known by the brand name Apresoline and is primarily used to treat high blood pressure (hypertension). However, it may also be prescribed for other conditions as determined by your healthcare provider.
